findingsVerbatim: I01 — Loader and parent do not share the same startup admission contract. **NOT ADDRESSED IN FULL.** The original executable-path/owner/mode mismatch is removed: F7:79–83 emits a seven-field binding; outer.mjs:41–51 opens the current kernel image; controls-boundary.py:31–49 and boundary.py:31–49 read the binding and inherited descriptor. Stage aliases now distinguish setup, binding, helper, parent and record failures. One concrete predicate still diverges. outer.mjs:45 applies a JavaScript regular expression directly to c.sourceTree without requiring a string. A JSON array containing one valid 40-hex string coerces to that string, passes this check, and has no independent environment equality check at :46. Both Python parents at :46 pass the array to re.fullmatch, which rejects it. For this malformed binding the Node entry proceeds to the parent instead of closing as binding_unavailable. Require the same primitive string type and shape at both boundaries. F7 itself constructs a string for a normal unaltered context. This residual did not cause the recorded setup failure.

**N01 / Important — F7 requires two different digests of the exact same matrix.** F7:76–78 pins the 19,174-byte matrix blob f646d4007f4348da75b0b5a99059246606c4d685 to SHA256 1b6f74a16aa37818fe51bdf3bdea2a1d3946a4198736ca3d630f4ba30b7f6039 and validates every helper, then demands SHA256 1ae00081c12e4267601557ee085537d67f6c644075a9ba2a7559334971e87d85 for those same bytes. The latter is the obsolete 71-row matrix. I independently hashed the new matrix as inert JSON bytes in RAM. The conjunctive gate cannot succeed, before materialization or runControls(). F7:84,262–263 converts a bootstrap exception to setup_unavailable. With both action outcomes success, this is consistent with the observed layer. The precise exception reached on that run was not traced; an earlier setup failure would produce the same receipt. Remove the independent stale literal or derive its comparison from the verified manifest, and compare every executable matrix-pin consumer to the actual matrix bytes as DATA before any new release.

**N02 / Important — The new outer rejects the real pinned Source schema on every source-qualified delivery.** outer.mjs:27 defines jsonFixed as JSON.stringify(parsed) === raw, excluding a final LF. outer.mjs:161–162 uses it on site-schema.json when delivery.sourceQualified is true; the same new code is in delivery-entry.sh:167. The pre-existing pinned site-schema.json blob 4871edc102386fe6db65c773e51c21ecb94897e3 (F7:76) is 12,651 bytes, SHA256 5b55423937bbe38a18f1bbb8196d8cd85336d81187810b8c5b5abe8a593c37fd, and is exactly canonical JSON **plus one LF**. This was independently checked as data. All valid-Source samples and source-qualified missing/invalid samples hit record_invalid before :167 can validate associations, including baseline A01 and the intended S01 mutant discriminant. Read this pinned metadata with its declared LF framing. Do not mutate frozen bytes or relax raw sample/evidence framing. This is an integration regression in the new outer, not a defect in the unchanged schema.

**N03 / Important — Two staged faults make M_OUTPUT permanently unknown if attempted.** controls.mjs:99 replaces boundary.py with a one-line import failure for B11; :115 unlinks it for E03. At :167 change() runs BEFORE mutant installation. M_OUTPUT at :174–176 unconditionally transforms that file, and :168 throws for missing needle/file. execute() at :202–205 turns each exception into unknown without running the case. At :215–216 even one such unknown forces the mutant's overall result to unknown. Applying only the matrix hash repair cannot yield the exact M_OUTPUT=[B05] known result. Apply the mutant to the pristine verified program first, then stage row-specific startup faults, retaining actual failures and unmeasured states honestly.

**N04 / Important — The new public validator accepts its schema and ordered-ID authority from files still writable by its captured helper, after the helper returns.** F7:80–81 initially hashes owner-writable 0600 helpers under an owner-writable 0700 directory. outer.mjs:54–69 runs the same-UID child first, then loads matrix.json and controls-schema.json; :160–165 repeats this pattern for delivery/envelope schemas. jsonFixed at :27 checks canonical encoding, not a trusted digest. The report's matrix hash at :71 is compared to a literal field of the report, not independently recomputed from the just-read authority. Concrete private-output counterexample: a faulty/substituted Python parent with the same access used by the staged parent-failure tests can append a key with a private string value to the sibling delivery schema's required/properties and emit a matching, context-correct, source-unqualified unavailable record with that key and status 23. :160,170–173 would reserialize and publish the private field. It does not need a valid Source-site record for this path. No such leak was measured. Pin the public schema/matrix bytes to an independent immutable anchor and use the verified in-memory values through final publication (including the declared framing of the site schema). Initial setup verification cannot secure a later writable reread; Root rejection after publication cannot withdraw bytes.

**N05 / Important — The new timeout layer can leave its separately sessioned grandchild alive.** outer.mjs:57–61 starts Python in a detached group and kills only that group after 5 s / 120 s. boundary.py:58–60 and controls-boundary.py:58–60 start their own Node in a NEW session and start their inner clocks after spawn, for the same 5 s / 120 s. If the outer timer fires first while the inner Node is stalled, the Python process can die before its own finally cleanup and the Node process is outside the killed group. The outer can then observe its Python pipes close and return while the grandchild continues. The new 90 s admission check in controls.mjs:9–10,211–216 limits normal harness admission. T01 at :127–130,194 supplies a pre-expired clock; it does not cover loss of the live supervising parent or a blocked delivery emitter. Keep fixed transport descendants in a killable containment group or supply an independent lifetime guarantee that survives supervisor death, with distinct nested time budgets. This concerns synthetic/transport processes only; no Native activity or orphan was observed.

**N06 / Important — The new cleanup can chmod an inode outside the synthetic root via a hard link.** controls.mjs:139–149 verifies path containment and skips symbolic links, but unconditionally chmods every owned regular file. A second directory entry in a generated case can reference an owned file outside the case. lstat's regular-file/UID predicate accepts it and chmod changes the shared inode's permissions at both entries. Hard links are already a supported fault fixture at :73. Its current fixture links two names inside the case; no external inode change was observed. File write permission is unnecessary to unlink an entry from an owned writable directory. Omit regular-file chmod or independently establish that every link is case-owned. This is new cleanup behavior, separate from the original excessive per-case retention.
